detail: fnn-acquire (io.lisp:2708) and fnn-open-live-store (io.lisp:4396) wrap acquisition and recovery in handler-case (error (e) (fnn-store-failed-open-close store e)). A non-error serious-condition (storage-condition on heap exhaustion during fnn-recover, sb-sys:interactive-interrupt) escapes without closing the store object they created; a caller such as fnn-command-probe (io.lisp:6264, cb6e45ac3), whose cleanup names its own unopened store, cannot reach it. The process exits right after on every current caller, so the kernel releases the lock and descriptors; the defect is the uncloseable store object and its close debt, not a durable effect. Fix: both handlers take serious-condition, as fnn-store-failed-open-close itself does; regression: a developer fault selector raising a storage-condition inside fnn-recover, observing the store's close (log and lock slots nil, close-debt recorded or none).
source: A21 audit of L17 lane/log-l4@cb6e45ac3 (probe fix F1), 2026-10-12
title: fnn-acquire and fnn-open-live-store close the store only on error, not on any serious-condition: a storage-condition or interrupt during the live open leaves the opened store unclosed
